newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber extends losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber extends losses at close.

text.p: Rubber prices in Malaysia extended losses at the close due to falls in Tokyo and an absence of active offtake from major consumers, dealers said.

"There was little business transacted. People are still waiting for the outcome of the South Korean tender," a dealer said, adding that Chinese buyers continued to look for cheaper levels for prompt SMR 20.
South Korea tendered to buy SMR 10 and 20, and latex rubber for nearby shipment.
Dealers offered SMR CV at 320 cents, SMR L at 300, SMR 10 at 251, SMR 20 at 249-250 and latex at 217-219 cents.
At the close, July RSS1 buyer eased 2.50 cents to 272 cents ($1.08) a kg and July SMR 20 buyer was down 1.50 cents at 251.
Local dealers are also seen covering while interest from Europe remained lacking after earlier covering ahead of the summer holidays.
The INRO five-day average was 205.93 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on June 23 from 207.25 on June 20. The daily indicator was 203.80 against 204.03.
